```{r loadData}
#### load variables
xlsx_file_path <- file.path(input_dir,paste0(params$study_name,"_list_of_vars.xlsx"))
tab_names<-openxlsx::getSheetNames(xlsx_file_path)
### list with separate element for each tab
list_of_vars <- lapply(tab_names,
                           openxlsx::read.xlsx,xlsxFile=xlsx_file_path)
names(list_of_vars) <- tab_names



xlsx_file_path <- file.path(input_dir,paste0(params$study_name,"_list_of_rawDatasets.xlsx"))
tab_names<-openxlsx::getSheetNames(xlsx_file_path)
### list with separate element for each tab
list_of_raw <- lapply(tab_names,
                           openxlsx::read.xlsx,xlsxFile=xlsx_file_path)
names(list_of_raw) <- tab_names

raw_df_TOA <- list_of_raw[["TOA"]] %>%
  ### add TOA_adj
    ### recalculate TOA_adj == all match when topped at 12 challenges
  dplyr::mutate(TOA_adj = ifelse(Infection_status == 0,
                                  TOA + 1,
                                  TOA),
                TOA_adj = ifelse(TOA_adj > 12, 12, TOA_adj)
  )
  

### raw data is wide format
phen_long <- list_of_raw[["data"]] %>%
  ### add TOA data
  dplyr::left_join(raw_df_TOA, by = c("Sample_ID","studyLetterForMS")) %>%
### add Sex
  dplyr::left_join(unique(list_of_raw[["metadata"]][,c("Sample_ID","Sex")]), by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  ### make longer
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!all_of(c(colnames(raw_df_TOA),"Sex")),names_to = "var_comp_time", values_to = "amount") %>%
  ## separate var_comp_time
  dplyr::mutate(variable = str_before_first(var_comp_time, "____"),
                Specimen = str_before_first(str_after_first(var_comp_time,"____"),"____"),
                Time_Point = str_after_last(var_comp_time,"____"),
                var_comp_time = NULL,
                Animal_comp_time = paste0("m",Sample_ID,"__",Specimen,"__",Time_Point),
                weeks_n = ifelse(grepl(paste(c("wk","Wk","Post"),collapse = '|'),Time_Point),
                                 as.numeric(1), ### if it's post, then 1
                                 as.numeric(0)),
                studyLetterForMS = factor(studyLetterForMS, c("studyA1","studyA2","studyB","studyC","studyD","studyE","studyF")),
                Group_simp = str_before_last(Group,"_") ###remove sex from Group
                )   %>%
##first remove na
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(amount))%>%
  arrange(Sample_ID, Specimen, variable, weeks_n) %>%
  group_by(Sample_ID, Specimen, variable) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(FC = 100*(amount / amount[1L]),
                delta = amount - amount [1L]) %>%
  ungroup() 
  


#phen_long <- readRDS(file = file.path(input_dir, paste0(params$study_name,"_phen_long.rds")))
#phen_long_forTOA <- readRDS(file = file.path(input_dir, paste0(params$study_name,"_phen_long_forTOA.rds")))
list_of_vars <- readRDS(file = file.path(input_dir, paste0(params$study_name,"_list_of_vars.rds")))


```

```{r summaryTable}
animal_df <- unique(raw_df_TOA[,c("Sample_ID","Group","studyLetterForMS")]) %>%
  ### rename since gender is included in group
  dplyr::mutate(Group_gender = Group)

animal_df_tab <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(animal_df$Group_gender, animal_df$studyLetterForMS)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Group_gender") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Group = str_before_last(Group_gender,"_"),
                Sex = str_after_last(Group_gender,"_"),
                Group_gender = NULL) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Group), Sex) %>%
  dplyr::relocate(Group, Sex)
  
animal_df_tab %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_zebra() %>%
  set_caption(caption = "Number of Animals from each study in each experimental group, used at some point in the manuscript")


###### prep lists
list_of_stats <- list()
list_of_plotted <- list()
### to collect formatted supp tables
suppTables_wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()

```

Total `r dim(animal_df)[1]` animals, with `r length(which(animal_df$studyLetterForMS != "Control_group"))` vaccinated and `r length(which(animal_df$studyLetterForMS == "Control_group"))` naive


*** **Ignoring ALFQA status for each of DNA or ALVAC groups = 2 groups** ***

## Supp Figure 1 (Study Setup) {.tabset}

### Which variables, which studies {.tabset}

```{r whichVarsTab, results='asis'}
var_types_list <- list("SuppFig1B_AvidityAbADCCEff"=c(list_of_vars[["ADCC_columns"]],list_of_vars[["eff_columns"]],list_of_vars[["Abs_columns"]]),
                       
                       "SuppFig1C_RectMucosaCells"=c(list_of_vars[["arifnew_NK"]],list_of_vars[["arifnew_mono"]],list_of_vars[["arifnew_DC"]]),
                       "SuppFig1D_PBMCcells"=c(list_of_vars[["massinew_mono"]],list_of_vars[["massinew_tcells"]]),
                       "SuppFig1E_CytoChemokines"=c(list_of_vars[["olink_columns"]])
                       
                       )



study_color_vec <- c(studyA1="gold2", #"lightsalmon", #Alum"orchid1" and ALFQA"gold2","darkorange1"
                    studyA2="#FF9FFB",
                     studyB="magenta3",
                    
                     
                     studyC="green1",
                     studyD="darkgreen",
                     studyE="dodgerblue3",
                     studyF="olivedrab")

### for each type of variable
for(curr_vt in names(var_types_list)){
  
  curr_summ <- phen_long %>%
    ###remove unneeded metadata,FC and delta etc.
    dplyr::select(studyLetterForMS,Animal_comp_time,variable, amount) %>%
    ### trim to only these vars
    dplyr::filter(variable %in% var_types_list[[curr_vt]]) %>%
    ### summarize how many datapoints we have that are not NA
    dplyr::group_by(studyLetterForMS, variable) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(non_na_count = sum(!is.na(amount))) %>%
    ### make wide
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "studyLetterForMS", values_from = "non_na_count")
  
  ### now generate df to have all the studies
  df_to_plot <- data.frame(variable = curr_summ$variable)
  
  ### now add in the columns from curr_sum
  for(curr_study in levels(phen_long$studyLetterForMS)[1:7]){
    
    if(length(which(grepl(curr_study,colnames(curr_summ)) == TRUE) == 1)){
      ### if has data, add the column from curr_summ
          df_to_plot <- df_to_plot %>%
      dplyr::left_join(curr_summ[,c("variable",curr_study)], by = "variable")
    }else{
      ### if not add all NAs
      df_to_plot <- df_to_plot %>%
        ### add column with all NA
        dplyr::left_join(data.frame(variable = curr_summ$variable,
                           new_study = rep(NA, length(curr_summ$variable))) %>%
                           `colnames<-`(c("variable",curr_study)),
                         by = "variable")
        
    }
    
    

  }
  
  cat("#### ",paste0(curr_vt),"\n")
cat("\n")


  ##### now swap in the study color if not na for plot
  df_to_plot2 <- df_to_plot %>%
    ### remove rows with only one study
    dplyr::filter_at(vars(studyA1:studyF), any_vars(!is.na(.))) %>%
    ## collect number of studies
    column_to_rownames("variable") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(numStudies = rowSums(!is.na(.)),
                  whichStudies = ifelse(!is.na(studyF),"first","next")) %>%
    rownames_to_column("variable") %>%
    ### make longer
    tidyr::pivot_longer(!c(variable,numStudies,whichStudies), names_to = "study", values_to = "value") %>%
    ## add color for non na values
    dplyr::mutate(study_have = ifelse(is.na(value),NA,study)) %>%
    ### remove unneeded columns
    dplyr::select(-value) %>%
    ## factorize to get order we want
    dplyr::mutate(study = factor(study, levels(phen_long$studyLetterForMS)[1:7])) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(whichStudies),numStudies,study, variable) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(variable = factor(variable, unique(variable)),
                  numStudies = NULL) 
  
  p <- df_to_plot2 %>% 
    ggplot( aes(x = study, y = variable, fill = study_have))+
    geom_tile(color = "black")+
    scale_fill_manual(values = study_color_vec)+
    ## no buffer out side plot
    scale_x_discrete(expand=c(0,0))+
    scale_y_discrete(expand=c(0,0))+
    theme_bw()+
    theme(axis.ticks = element_blank(), legend.position="none")
  
  plot(p)
  
   
  cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
  
  list_of_plotted[[paste0(curr_vt)]] <- df_to_plot2

     cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
 
}

 
  cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!



```





## Figure 1 (TOA) {.tabset}


### Fig 1C: combo DNA (male+female) vs combo Naive (male+female)

ignoring ALFQA

```{r DNAvsNaiveIgnoreALFQA_setup}
#### set groups and order
group_var_to_use <- "Group_ignoreALFQA"
groups_to_use <- c("Naive","DNA")
colors_to_use <- c("grey50","darkorange1")

### if need to trim out any groups
phen_long_to_use1 <- raw_df_TOA


```

```{r TOA, results='asis'}

####### select animals for the aquistion curve
# phen_long_to_use <- phen_long_to_use1 %>%
#   dplyr::filter(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use) %in% groups_to_use) %>%
#   dplyr::select(c(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use),Study_number,Sample_ID,TOA_adj,Infection_status)) %>%
#   unique(.) %>% 
#   dplyr::arrange(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use),Sample_ID) %>%
#   
#     ### collapse rows and take first value ***need to see if this is correct**
#   dplyr::group_by(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use), Sample_ID) %>%
#   dplyr::reframe(across(everything(), ~ dplyr::first(.))) %>% 
#   ungroup()


summ <- phen_long_to_use1 %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(status = recode(Infection_status, "0"=0,"1"=1), ## status needs to be 0,1
                time = as.numeric(TOA_adj),
                vaccine = factor(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use), groups_to_use))


## survival function
#Surv(summ$time, summ$status) #calculates censored samples (i.e. that never had infection in time period observed)

### set title for 2 or 3 groups
if(length(groups_to_use)>2){
  title_to_use <- paste0(groups_to_use[1]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[1]))[1],"; ",
                      groups_to_use[2]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[2]))[1],"; ",
                      groups_to_use[3]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[3]))[1])
}else{
   title_to_use <- paste0(groups_to_use[1]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[1]))[1],"; ",
                      groups_to_use[2]," n=",dim(filter(summ, vaccine == groups_to_use[2]))[1])
 
}


survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ vaccine, data=summ) %>%
  ggsurvfit(linewidth=1)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:12, expand=c(0.02,0))+
  scale_y_continuous(label = scales::percent, breaks=seq(0,1, by=0.2), expand=c(0.015,0))+
  labs(title = title_to_use,
       x = "Weeks",
       y = "% uninfected macaques")+
  scale_color_manual(values=colors_to_use)+
  scale_fill_manual(values=colors_to_use)+
  add_confidence_interval()+
  add_pvalue(location = "annotation")+
  ggsurvfit::add_risktable(times=c(seq(0,12,1)))+
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), 
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
        )





 cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!


```

```{r 2Groups_prep}
                                  "group2"=c("ALVAC"),
```

MW test


```{r studiesUsedTable}
### number of animals per study group
num_animals_per_study <- curr_phen_long %>%
  ### remove NA in amount
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(amount)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID,Study_number,Group) %>% 
  unique(.) 

curr_phen_long %>%
  ### remove NA in amount
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(amount)) %>%
  ### add number of animals
  dplyr::left_join(as.data.frame(table(num_animals_per_study$Study_number, num_animals_per_study$Group)) %>%
                     ## rename to useful
                     dplyr::rename(Study_number=Var1,Group=Var2,NumAnimals=Freq),
                   by = c("Study_number","Group")) %>%
  ### add gender to group
  dplyr::mutate(Group_gender = Group,
                Study_number = ifelse(is.na(Study_number),"Control",Study_number)) %>%
  dplyr::select(Group_gender,Study_number,studyLetterForMS,NumAnimals) %>%
  unique(.) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Group = str_before_last(Group_gender,"_"),
                Sex = str_after_last(Group_gender,"_"),
                Group_gender = NULL) %>%
  dplyr::relocate(Group, Sex) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Group),Sex) %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_zebra() %>%
  set_caption(caption = paste0("Studies used in ",fig_name_to_use))
```


```{r diffBetweenGroups, results='asis', fig.height=18, fig.width=8}

### for each dataset type

for(curr_ds in ds_to_use){
  cat("#### ",paste0(curr_ds," {.tabset}"),"\n")
  cat('\n')
  
  
  ## full_df only has the variables in columns and the factorized group (plus any other covariates if they are in the model)
  
  full_df <- curr_phen_long %>%
    ## trim to only Animal_comp_time, var and curr_ds
    dplyr::select(c(Animal_comp_time,variable,!!rlang::sym(curr_ds))) %>%
    ## move comp and timepoint to var
    dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = str_before_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),
                  var_comp_time = paste0(variable,"__",str_after_first(Animal_comp_time,"__")),
                  Animal_comp_time = NULL,
                  variable = NULL) %>%
    ## make wider
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var_comp_time", values_from = all_of(curr_ds)) %>%
    ## remove columns with only NA
    dplyr::select(where(function(x) !all(is.na(x)))) %>%
    ### add in group
    dplyr::left_join(data.frame(unique(phen_long[,c("Sample_ID",group_var_to_use)])) %>%
                       dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = paste0("m",Sample_ID)), by = "Sample_ID") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Group_to_use=!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use)) %>%
    column_to_rownames("Sample_ID") %>%
    ### factorize group
    dplyr::mutate(Group_f = factor(Group_to_use, intersect(
      names(group_colors_to_use),
      unique(data.frame(curr_phen_long)[,group_var_to_use])))) %>%
    dplyr::select(-Group_to_use)
  
  
  
  p_value_df1 <- data.frame("rowname"=colnames(full_df)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(rowname != "Group_f")
  
  ######### if have any columns at all
  if(dim(full_df)[2]>1){
    
    
    
    
    for (g in 1:nrow(groups_to_compare)){
      
      
      
      
      ###### only if you have both groups
      if(length(which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g])) != 0 &
         length(which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g])) != 0){
        
        
        ## wilcoxon for pairwise differences
        
        ## generate matrix with only variables for stats 
        Assay_mat <- as.matrix(full_df[,p_value_df1$rowname])
        
        ## kruskal test for if there are differences between any groups - not necessary since only 2 groups with these timepoints
        # kruskal_p_raw <- apply(Assay_mat, 2, function(x) kruskal.test(x ~ Group_f, data = full_df)$p.value)
        # kruskal_p_adj <- p.adjust(kruskal_p_raw, method = 'BH')
        
        
        
        
        ## if there are no NAs for the group comparison (i.e. we have animals in both groups for the assay/timepoint)
        if(length(which(is.na(Assay_mat[rownames(full_df)[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g] | 
                                                                full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g])]
                                        ,]))) == 0)
          #then calculate as usual
        {
          curr_p_raw <- apply(Assay_mat, 2, function(x) wilcox.test(x[Group_f %in% c(
            groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])] ~ Group_f[Group_f %in% c(
              groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])], data = full_df)$p.value)
          curr_p_adj <- p.adjust(curr_p_raw, method = 'BH') 
          ##### since have zeros, can't use the wilcox function
          # curr_est <- apply(Assay_mat, 2, function(x) wilcox.test(x[Group_f %in% c(
          #   groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])] ~ Group_f[Group_f %in% c(
          #     groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])], data = full_df, conf.int = TRUE)$estimate)
          #### https://aakinshin.net/posts/r-hodges-lehmann-problems/
          
          ###### first define function
          hl <- function(x, y = NULL) {
            if (is.null(y)) {
              walsh <- outer(x, x, "+") / 2
              median(walsh[lower.tri(walsh, diag = TRUE)], na.rm = TRUE)
            } else {
              median(outer(x, y, "-"), na.rm = TRUE)
            }
          }
          
          #### then generate the vector
          curr_est <- c()
          curr_x_len <- c()
          curr_y_len <- c()
          for(i in colnames(Assay_mat)){
            x <- full_df[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g]),i]
            y <- full_df[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g]),i]
            ce <- hl(x, y)
            names(ce) <- i
            curr_est <- c(curr_est,ce)
            curr_x_len <- c(curr_x_len,length(x))
            curr_y_len <- c(curr_y_len,length(y))
          }
          
          
          #### combine to df
          
          curr_p_df <- data.frame(curr_p_raw, curr_p_adj, curr_est,
                                  curr_x_len,curr_y_len) %>%
            rownames_to_column() 
          colnames(curr_p_df) <- c("rowname",
                                   
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_raw"),
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_adj"),
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__est"),
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup2"),
                                   paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup1")
          )
          
          ## but if there are all NAs for a group (i.e. one of the groups is missing the assay/timepoint), remove rows from Assay mat that have NAs (i.e. assay/timepoints that only have one of the groups to compare)
        } else {
          ### removes column if rows have NAs
          #new_curr_df <- full_df[,colSums(is.na(full_df))==0] %>%
          #  column_to_rownames("ID")
          
          ## since a few assays have a stray NA in the one group
          ### trim to only the groups being compared
          trim_df1 <- full_df[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g]),] #%>% dplyr::select(-Group_f)
          columns_with_noNAs1 <- colnames(trim_df1)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df1)) == 0)]
          columns_with_someNAs1 <- colnames(trim_df1)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df1)) > 0 & colSums(is.na(trim_df1)) < dim(trim_df1)[1])]
          columns_with_allNAs1 <- colnames(trim_df1)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df1)) == dim(trim_df1)[1])]
          
          
          trim_df2 <- full_df[which(full_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g]),] #%>% dplyr::select(-Group_f)
          columns_with_noNAs2 <- colnames(trim_df2)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df2)) == 0)]
          columns_with_someNAs2 <- colnames(trim_df2)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df2)) > 0 & colSums(is.na(trim_df2)) < dim(trim_df2)[1])]
          columns_with_allNAs2 <- colnames(trim_df2)[which(colSums(is.na(trim_df2)) == dim(trim_df2)[1])]
          
          #### if there are any columns with data for both groups
          if(length(intersect(c(columns_with_noNAs1,columns_with_someNAs1),c(columns_with_noNAs2,columns_with_someNAs2))) > 1){
            
            new_curr_df <- full_df[,intersect(c(columns_with_noNAs1,columns_with_someNAs1),c(columns_with_noNAs2,columns_with_someNAs2))] %>%
              ### also remove rows will all NA data, can't calculate est
              filter(if_any(!Group_f, ~ !is.na(.)))
            new_Assay_mat <- data.matrix(new_curr_df[,-which(colnames(new_curr_df) == "Group_f")])
            
            ### for the case where it is a single column
            colnames(new_Assay_mat) <- colnames(new_curr_df)[-which(colnames(new_curr_df) == "Group_f")]
            
            
            
            
            curr_p_raw <- apply(new_Assay_mat, 2, function(x) wilcox.test(x[Group_f %in% c(
              groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])] ~ Group_f[Group_f %in% c(
                groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])], data = new_curr_df)$p.value)
            curr_p_adj <- p.adjust(curr_p_raw, method = 'BH') 
            # curr_est <- apply(new_Assay_mat, 2, function(x) wilcox.test(x[Group_f %in% c(
            #    groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])] ~ Group_f[Group_f %in% c(
            #      groups_to_compare$group1[g], groups_to_compare$group2[g])], data = new_curr_df, conf.int = TRUE)$estimate)
            
            ###### first define function
            hl <- function(x, y = NULL) {
              if (is.null(y)) {
                walsh <- outer(x, x, "+") / 2
                median(walsh[lower.tri(walsh, diag = TRUE)], na.rm = TRUE)
              } else {
                median(outer(x, y, "-"), na.rm = TRUE)
              }
            }
            
            #### then generate the vector
            curr_est <- c()
            curr_x_len <- c()
            curr_y_len <- c()
            for(i in colnames(new_Assay_mat)){
              x <- new_curr_df[which(new_curr_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group2[g]),i]
              y <- new_curr_df[which(new_curr_df$Group_f == groups_to_compare$group1[g]),i]
              ce <- hl(x, y)
              names(ce) <- i
              curr_est <- c(curr_est,ce)
              curr_x_len <- c(curr_x_len,length(x))
              curr_y_len <- c(curr_y_len,length(y))
            }
            
            
            
            #### combine to df
            
            curr_p_df <- data.frame(curr_p_raw, curr_p_adj, curr_est,
                                    curr_x_len,curr_y_len) %>%
              rownames_to_column() 
            colnames(curr_p_df) <- c("rowname",
                                     
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_raw"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_adj"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__est"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup2"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup1")
            )
            
            
          }else{
            #### so that these definitely don't get carried over
            curr_p_raw <- NA
            curr_p_adj <- NA
            curr_est <- NA
            curr_x_len <- NA
            curr_y_len <- NA
            
            #### combine to df
            
            curr_p_df <- data.frame(matrix(nrow=0, ncol=6))
            colnames(curr_p_df) <- c("rowname",
                                     
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_raw"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_adj"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__est"),
                                     
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup2"),
                                     paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup1"))
            curr_p_df$rowname <- as.character(curr_p_df$rowname)
            
          }
          
        }
        
        
      }else{
        #### so that these definitely don't get carried over
        curr_p_raw <- NA
        curr_p_adj <- NA
        curr_est <- NA
        curr_x_len <- NA
        curr_y_len <- NA
        
        #### combine to df
        
        curr_p_df <- data.frame(matrix(nrow=0, ncol=6))
        colnames(curr_p_df) <- c("rowname",
                                 
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_raw"),
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__p_adj"),
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__est"),
                                 
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup2"),
                                 paste0(groups_to_compare$name[g],"__Ngroup1"))
        curr_p_df$rowname <- as.character(curr_p_df$rowname)
      }
      
      
      ### add these groups to compare to the p_value_df1
      p_value_df1 <- dplyr::full_join(p_value_df1, curr_p_df, by="rowname") 
      
      
      
      
      
    }
    
    
    
    
    ## format p values
    p_value_df1 <- p_value_df1 %>%
      column_to_rownames() %>%
      ## set sig figs
      mutate_all(signif, 2) %>%
      rownames_to_column()
    
    
    
    
    ## add up/down with sig columns 
    for(curr_comp in groups_to_compare$name){
      curr_df <- p_value_df1[,c("rowname",colnames(p_value_df1)[grepl(paste0(curr_comp,"__"),colnames(p_value_df1))])] %>%
        `colnames<-`(c("rowname","p_raw","p_adj","est","Ngroup2","Ngroup1")) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(dir = factor(ifelse(p_raw < 0.05, ifelse(est > 0, "up, p < 0.05","down, p < 0.05"),
                                          ifelse(p_raw < 0.1, ifelse(est > 0, "up, p < 0.1","down, p < 0.1"),
                                                 ifelse(p_raw>0.05,"not_sig","no_test"))),
                                   c("up, p < 0.05","up, p < 0.1","not_sig","down, p < 0.1","down, p < 0.05","no_test"))) %>%
        dplyr::select(-c(p_raw,p_adj,est,Ngroup2,Ngroup1)) %>%
        `colnames<-`(c("rowname",paste0(curr_comp,"__dir")))
      
      p_value_df1 <- dplyr::left_join(p_value_df1, curr_df, by = "rowname")
      
    }
    
    
    ## format p values
    p_value_df1 <- p_value_df1 %>%
      column_to_rownames() 
    
    
    
    
    
    
    ################################################ NOW plot heatmaps ################################################
    #### collect timepoints for this curr_var_set
    
    ### sort for olink
    if(grepl("olink",curr_var_set)){
      #tps_for_thisSet <- c("Baseline","wk12_24or72h","wk13")
      tps_for_thisSet <- c("Baseline","wk12_24or72h")
    }else{
      tps_for_thisSet <- unique(str_after_last(rownames(p_value_df1),"__"))
    }
    
    vars_to_use <- sort(unique(str_before_last(rownames(p_value_df1),"__")))
    
    sig_assay_df <- p_value_df1 %>%
      rownames_to_column() %>%
      ### add factored timepoint
      dplyr::mutate(Time = factor(str_after_last(rowname,"__"), tps_for_thisSet),
                    variable = factor(str_before_last(rowname,"__"),vars_to_use)) 
    
    #### if FC or delta, remove baseline
    if(curr_ds != "amount"){
      sig_assay_df <- sig_assay_df %>%
        dplyr::filter(Time != "Baseline")
      
      
      cat(" ", paste0("TRUE ", curr_ds),"\n")
      cat("\n")
      ### also set breakscales
      row_scale_set <- "none"
      if(curr_ds == "FC"){
        mycols <- colorRampPalette(c("blue3","white","red3"))(1000)
        range <- 100
        breakscale <- c(0,
                        seq(0.001,99.99, length.out=length(mycols)/2-1),
                        seq(100,399, length.out=length(mycols)/2),
                        400)
        
      }else{
        ### for delta
        mycols <- colorRampPalette(c("blue3","white","red3"))(1000)
        range <- 100
        breakscale <- c(-1*range,seq(-.9*range,.9*range, length.out=length(mycols)-1),1*range)
        
      }
    }else{
      
      cat(" ", paste0("ROWSCALED"),"\n")
      cat("\n")
      row_scale_set <- "row"
      mycols <- colorRampPalette(c("blue4","white","red4"))(1000)
      range <- 2
      breakscale <- c(-1*range,seq(-.9*range,.9*range, length.out=length(mycols)-1),1*range)
      
      
    }
    
    #### dir columns
    dir_columns <- rev(colnames(sig_assay_df)[grepl("dir",colnames(sig_assay_df))])
    
    ##### annotation for rows, first listed will be closest to the heatmap (right side of ann cols), last will be on the left edge of the plot
    annotation_row = sig_assay_df[,c(dir_columns,"Time","variable","rowname")] %>%
      ### add simpler rowname with out the annotation
      #dplyr::mutate(rowname_clean = str_before_first(rowname,"xx__")) %>%
      column_to_rownames() 
    
    
    
    ###### annotation for columns
    annotation_col <- full_df %>%
      dplyr::select(Group_f) %>%
      ## arrange
      dplyr::arrange(Group_f)
    
    
    ##### for baseline also sort by dir
    
    if(grepl("base",fig_name_to_use)){
      #### set orders to use
      hm_orders_to_use <- list(
        "by Assay, timepoint, dir"=c("variable","Time",dir_columns),
        "by timepoint, dir, Assay"=c("Time",dir_columns,"variable")
      )
      
      
    }else{
      #### set orders to use
      hm_orders_to_use <- list(
        "by Assay, timepoint, dir"=c("variable","Time",dir_columns)
      )
      
    }
    
    ####### set annotation colors 
    ### first for time
    timepoints_df <- data.frame("tp"=c("Baseline","wk12_24or72h","wk13","wk13_14","wk14","wk14_15","wk17","Post"),
                                "color"=c("grey95",
                                          "lemonchiffon",
                                          "lemonchiffon3",
                                          "bisque1",
                                          "bisque2",
                                          "bisque2",
                                          "bisque3",
                                          "bisque4")) %>%
      column_to_rownames("tp")
    
    
    
    time_for_anncolors <- timepoints_df[tps_for_thisSet,]
    names(time_for_anncolors) <- tps_for_thisSet
    
    
    ####
    
    
    annotation_colors=list()
    annotation_colors[["Group_f"]] <- group_colors_to_use
    
    annotation_colors[["Time"]] <- time_for_anncolors
    for(curr_dir in dir_columns){
      annotation_colors[[paste0(curr_dir)]] <- c("up, p < 0.05"="red2","up, p < 0.1"="lightpink",not_sig="black",
                                                 "down, p < 0.1"="skyblue","down, p < 0.05"="blue2",no_test="white")
    }
    
    
    # hmo <- names(hm_orders_to_use)[1]
    
    
    for(hmo in names(hm_orders_to_use)){
      
      if(grepl("base",fig_name_to_use)){
        cat("##### ", paste0(hmo," {.tabset}"),"\n")
        cat("\n")
      }else{
        cat("##### ", paste0("heatmaps {.tabset}"),"\n")
        cat("\n")
      }
      
      
      cat("###### ", paste0("untrimmed, ",hmo," "),"\n")
      cat("\n")
      
      
      
      ### arrange rows by order to use
      curr_ann_row1 <- dplyr::arrange(annotation_row,  annotation_row[,hm_orders_to_use[[hmo]]]) 
      
      tmp <- full_df %>%
        ##remove Group_f
        dplyr::select(-Group_f) %>% 
        ## transpose to get columns = animals, rows = variables
        t() %>%
        data.frame() 
      
      tmp2 <-  tmp[rownames(curr_ann_row1),intersect(rownames(annotation_col),colnames(tmp))] %>%
        ### remove columns with all NA
        dplyr::select(where(function(.) any(!is.na(.))))
      
      ### set the gaps for the rows from first element of orders, except if assay
      if(hm_orders_to_use[[hmo]][1] != "Assay"){
        gaps_df <- data.frame(table(curr_ann_row1[,hm_orders_to_use[[hmo]][1]])) %>%
          mutate(cumsum = cumsum(Freq))
        if(length(unique(gaps_df$Freq)) ==1){
          if(unique(gaps_df$Freq) == 1){
            gaps_row_to_use <- 0
          }else{
            gaps_row_to_use <- unique(gaps_df$cumsum)
          }
          
        }else{
          gaps_row_to_use <- unique(gaps_df$cumsum)
        }
        
      }else{
        #gaps_df <- data.frame("cumsum"=c(0))
        gaps_row_to_use <- 0
      }
      
      #### gaps for column timepoints
      
      gaps_dfcol <- data.frame(table(annotation_col[colnames(tmp2),"Group_f"])) %>%
        dplyr::arrange(Var1) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(cumsum = cumsum(Freq))     
      
      
      
      
      ### remove variable so not plotted
      curr_ann_row <- curr_ann_row1%>%
        dplyr::select(-variable)
      
      # 
      if(grepl("olink",curr_var_set)){
        row_font_size <- 3
      }else{
        row_font_size <- 7
      }
      
      
      annotation_col_for_plot <- annotation_col %>% 
        rownames_to_column() %>% 
        dplyr::filter(rowname %in% colnames(tmp2)) %>% 
        column_to_rownames() %>%
        dplyr::arrange("Group_f")
      
      hc <-
        pheatmap(tmp2[,rownames(annotation_col_for_plot)],
                 scale=row_scale_set, 
                 na_col = "grey70",
                 cluster_cols=FALSE, 
                 cluster_rows = FALSE,
                 fontsize_row = row_font_size,
                 fontsize_col = 7,
                 gaps_col =unique(gaps_dfcol$cumsum),
                 gaps_row = gaps_row_to_use,
                 col=mycols, breaks=breakscale, 
                 clustering_method="ward.D2",
                 annotation_col = annotation_col_for_plot, 
                 annotation_row = curr_ann_row,
                 annotation_colors = annotation_colors)
```

```{r suppTable, results='asis'}
hex_to_rgba <- function(hex, alpha = 1) {

  sprintf("rgba(%d,%d,%d,%.3f)", rgb[1, ], rgb[2, ], rgb[3, ], alpha)
}

  blend_with_white <- function(hex, alpha) {
  # hex: character vector of "#RRGGBB"
  # alpha: numeric vector in [0,1] same length as hex
  stopifnot(length(hex) == length(alpha))

  rgb <- grDevices::col2rgb(hex)              # 3 x N
  alpha <- pmin(pmax(alpha, 0), 1)            # clamp

  # apply alpha per column
  blended <- sweep(rgb, 2, alpha, `*`) + sweep(matrix(255, 3, ncol(rgb)), 2, (1 - alpha), `*`)
  blended <- round(blended)

  sprintf("#%02X%02X%02X", blended[1, ], blended[2, ], blended[3, ])
}

# alpha by time (only baseline timepoint lighter)
time_levels <- levels(summary_df$Time)
alpha_by_time <- setNames(rep(1, length(time_levels)), time_levels)
alpha_by_time[["Baseline"]] <- 0.25



# compute per-row solid fill hex (alpha simulated on white)
summary_df_xlsx <- summary_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    fill_hex = blend_with_white(
      hex   = group_colors_to_use_hex[Group],
      alpha = alpha_by_time[as.character(Time)]
    )
  )
  
###### created earlier
  #suppTables_wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()

sheet_nm <- paste0(supptab_name,"_with",fig_name_to_use)

# add sheet
openxlsx::addWorksheet(suppTables_wb, sheet_nm)

# write data (drop helper column)
openxlsx::writeData(
  suppTables_wb,
  sheet = sheet_nm,
  x = summary_df_xlsx %>% dplyr::select(-fill_hex),
  withFilter = TRUE
)

# build row index map (Excel rows = data row + header)
fill_map <- summary_df_xlsx %>%
  dplyr::mutate(excel_row = dplyr::row_number() + 1) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(fill_hex) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(rows = list(excel_row), .groups = "drop")

# apply row fills (block-wise)
for (k in seq_len(nrow(fill_map))) {
  style_k <- openxlsx::createStyle(fgFill = fill_map$fill_hex[k])

  openxlsx::addStyle(
    suppTables_wb,
    sheet = sheet_nm,
    style = style_k,
    rows = unlist(fill_map$rows[k]),
    cols = 1:(ncol(summary_df_xlsx) - 1),
    gridExpand = TRUE,
    stack = TRUE
  )
}

# freeze header
openxlsx::freezePane(
  suppTables_wb,
  sheet = sheet_nm,
  firstRow = TRUE
)

# autosize columns
openxlsx::setColWidths(
  suppTables_wb,
  sheet = sheet_nm,
  cols = 1:(ncol(summary_df_xlsx) - 1),
  widths = "auto"
)

# bold header
header_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold")
openxlsx::addStyle(
  suppTables_wb,
  sheet = sheet_nm,
  style = header_style,
  rows = 1,
  cols = 1:(ncol(summary_df_xlsx) - 1),
  gridExpand = TRUE,
  stack = TRUE
)
```

```{r AssocWithTOA, results='asis', fig.height=20, fig.width=18}

### for each dataset type

for(curr_ds in ds_to_use){
  cat("#### ",paste0(curr_ds," {.tabset}"),"\n")
  cat('\n')
  
  
  Corr_name <- paste0(Corr_name_base,"_",curr_var_set,"_",curr_ds)
  
  ## full_df only has the variables in columns and the factorized group (plus any other covariates if they are in the model)
  
  full_df <- curr_phen_long %>%
    ## trim to only Animal_comp_time, var and curr_ds
    dplyr::select(c(Animal_comp_time,variable, !!rlang::sym(curr_ds))) %>%
    ## move comp and timepoint to var
    dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = str_before_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),
                  var_comp_time = paste0(variable,"__",str_after_first(Animal_comp_time,"__")),
                  Animal_comp_time = NULL,
                  variable = NULL) %>%
    ## make wider
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var_comp_time", values_from = all_of(curr_ds)) %>%
    ## remove columns with only NA
    dplyr::select(where(function(x) !all(is.na(x)))) %>%
    ### add in group & TOA
    dplyr::left_join(data.frame(unique(phen_long[,c("Sample_ID","TOA_adj",group_var_to_use)])) %>%
                       dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = paste0("m",Sample_ID)) %>%
                       ### collapse rows and take first value ***need to see if this is correct**
                       dplyr::group_by(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use), Sample_ID) %>%
                       dplyr::reframe(across(everything(), ~ dplyr::first(.))) %>% 
                       ungroup(), 
                     by = "Sample_ID") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Group_to_use=!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use)) %>%
    column_to_rownames("Sample_ID") %>%
    ### factorize group
    dplyr::mutate(Group_f = factor(Group_to_use, intersect(
      names(group_colors_to_use),
      unique(data.frame(curr_phen_long)[,group_var_to_use])))) %>%
    dplyr::select(-Group_to_use)
  
  
  #### only if have any variables with same animals as TOA
  if(dim(full_df)[2] > 2){
    
    ### for each group separately
    ### prep to collect
    corr_df_combo <- data.frame()
    
    for(curr_group in names(group_colors_to_use)){
      
      
      #curr_df1: rows = samples, columns = variables
      #curr_df2: rows = samples, columns = TAO
      
      
      curr_df1 <- full_df %>%
        ## filter to only this group
        dplyr::filter(Group_f == curr_group) %>%
        ## trim to only the variable columns
        dplyr::select(-c(TOA_adj, Group_f))
      
      curr_df2 <- full_df %>%
        ## filter to only this group
        dplyr::filter(Group_f == curr_group) %>%
        ## trim to only the variable columns
        dplyr::select(TOA_adj) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(TOA_adj = as.numeric(TOA_adj))
      
      ########## do correlation with psych package since much faster
      sp <- psych::corr.test(as.matrix(signif(curr_df1,7)), as.matrix(signif(curr_df2,7)), method = cor_method,
                             use="pairwise",
                             adjust="none",ci=FALSE)
      
      cor_mat <- sp$r
      cor_test_mat <- data.frame(sp$p)
      
      ## adj p for multiple comparisons by BH over assays
      cor_test_adj_mat <- cor_test_mat #duplicate dataframe to replace values
      for(curr_assay in colnames(curr_df1)) {
        cor_test_adj_mat[curr_assay,] <- p.adjust(cor_test_mat[curr_assay,], method = "BH")
      }
      
      
      #### also combine to dataframe since only one columns
      corr_df <- dplyr::left_join(data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
                                    rownames_to_column() %>%
                                    dplyr::rename(R_value=TOA_adj),
                                  data.frame(cor_test_mat) %>%
                                    rownames_to_column() %>%
                                    dplyr::rename(raw_p=TOA_adj),
                                  by = "rowname") %>%
        dplyr::left_join(data.frame(cor_test_adj_mat) %>%
                           rownames_to_column() %>%
                           dplyr::rename(adj_p=TOA_adj),
                         by = "rowname") %>%
        ### add columns
        dplyr::mutate(
          ### set R_value to NA if p is NA i.e there were only 2 datapoints, some how the R is calculated but the p is not
          R_value = ifelse(is.na(raw_p),NA,R_value),
          dir = ifelse(R_value > 0 & raw_p < 0.05,
                       "up", 
                       ifelse(R_value < 0 & raw_p < 0.05,
                              "down","not_sig")),
          Time = str_after_last(rowname, "__"),
          var_comp = str_before_last(rowname,"__"),
          Group = paste0(curr_group)) 
      
      
      corr_df_combo <- rbind(corr_df_combo, corr_df)
      
    }
    
    ### if FC or delta, remove baselines
    if(curr_ds != "amount"){
      corr_df_combo <- corr_df_combo %>% 
        dplyr::filter(Time != "Baseline")
    }
    
    ### save stats
    list_of_stats[[paste0(Corr_name_base,"_",str_remove_all(curr_var_set,"_columns"),"_",
                          substring(curr_ds,1,2) ## trim to 2 letters since too long for excel tab name
    )]] <- corr_df_combo
    
    # saveRDS(corr_df_combo, file = file.path(outputRData_dir, 
    #                                                               paste0(Corr_name,"_", cor_method,"_CoefPvals_untrimmed.rds")))
    
    
    cat("\n")
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
    
    
    ################## now plot sig correlations for all groups
    
    
    
    if(length(group_colors_to_use) == 2){
      #### set low/high range
      low_range <- data.frame(rowname="range_set_low",
                              DNA=as.numeric(1),
                              ALVAC=as.numeric(1))
      
      
      high_range <- data.frame(rowname="range_set_high",
                               DNA=as.numeric(1),
                               ALVAC=as.numeric(1))
      
      
      
      
      low_Rrange <- data.frame(rowname="range_set_low",
                               DNA=as.numeric(-1),
                               ALVAC=as.numeric(-1))
      
      
      high_Rrange <- data.frame(rowname="range_set_high",
                                DNA=as.numeric(1),
                                ALVAC=as.numeric(1))
    }else{
      #### set low/high range
      low_range <- data.frame(rowname="range_set_low",
                              studyA1=as.numeric(1),
                              studyA2=as.numeric(1),
                              studyB=as.numeric(1),
                              studyC=as.numeric(1),
                              studyD=as.numeric(1),
                              studyE=as.numeric(1),
                              #studyF=as.numeric(1)
                              )
      
      
      high_range <- data.frame(rowname="range_set_high",
                               studyA1=as.numeric(1),
                              studyA2=as.numeric(1),
                              studyB=as.numeric(1),
                              studyC=as.numeric(1),
                              studyD=as.numeric(1),
                              studyE=as.numeric(1),
                              #studyF=as.numeric(1)
                              )
      
      
      
      
      low_Rrange <- data.frame(rowname="range_set_low",
                               studyA1=as.numeric(-1),
                              studyA2=as.numeric(-1),
                              studyB=as.numeric(-1),
                              studyC=as.numeric(-1),
                              studyD=as.numeric(-1),
                              studyE=as.numeric(-1),
                              #studyF=as.numeric(-1)
                              )
      
      
      high_Rrange <- data.frame(rowname="range_set_high",
                                studyA1=as.numeric(1),
                              studyA2=as.numeric(1),
                              studyB=as.numeric(1),
                              studyC=as.numeric(1),
                              studyD=as.numeric(1),
                              studyE=as.numeric(1),
                              #studyF=as.numeric(1)
                              )
      
      
    }
    
    
    
    
    cor_test_mat_for_plot <- corr_df_combo %>%
      ### trim to only R values
      dplyr::select(rowname,raw_p,Group) %>%
      ## replace NaN with na
      dplyr::mutate(raw_p = ifelse(is.nan(raw_p),NA,raw_p)) %>%
      ## make wider
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "Group",values_from = "raw_p") %>%
      
      column_to_rownames() %>%
      ## filter to only vars that are sig in at least one group
      dplyr::filter_at(vars(everything(.)), any_vars(. < 0.05)) %>%
      rownames_to_column() %>%
      #### add dummy row to set square size range
      add_row(low_range) %>%
      add_row(high_range) %>%
      column_to_rownames() %>%
      as.matrix() 
    
    cor_mat_for_plot <- corr_df_combo %>%
      ### trim to only R values
      dplyr::select(rowname,R_value,Group) %>%
      ## make wider
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "Group",values_from = "R_value") %>%
      ### filter to only sig vars
      dplyr::filter(rowname %in% rownames(cor_test_mat_for_plot)) %>%
      #### add dummy row to set square size range
      add_row(low_Rrange) %>%
      add_row(high_Rrange) %>%
      column_to_rownames() %>%
      as.matrix()
    
    
    
    
    if(length(which(cor_test_mat_for_plot <  as.numeric(ann_pval_level))) == 0){
      
      
      cat(" ",paste0("no variables with p < ",ann_pval_level),"\n")
      cat('\n')
      
      
    }else{
      
      
      cat("##### ",paste0(" corrplot"),"\n")
      cat('\n')
      
      #### otherwise can use the stars
      corrplot::corrplot(cor_mat_for_plot, method = 'square', 
                         is.corr = FALSE, #since not symmetric
                         p.mat = cor_test_mat_for_plot,
                         sig.level = as.numeric(ann_pval_level), 
                         insig='label_sig',  #set p < 0.05 to blank
                         pch.cex = pch_cex, pch.col = 'white',tl.col = 'black',tl.cex=tl_cex,
                         ##legend
                         cl.ratio = cl_ratio, #cl.cex = 2,
                         #addCoef.col ='grey80', 
                         #number.cex = 0.5, #add corr coeff to sig circles
                         #order = order, ## CANNOT ORDER ASSYMMETRIC
                         col = colorRampPalette(c("gold4","white","seagreen4"))(200), ### change colors so don't match DNA
                         # col = (COL2('PuOr',1000)), ##make orange NEGATIVE
                         col.lim = c(-1,1) ##set limits to be the same across plots
                         # title = vaccine_groups[i], mar=c(0,0,1,0) # http://stackoverflow.com/a/14754408/54964
      )
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
      
      
      cat("##### ",paste0(" scatterplots {.active}"),"\n")
      cat('\n')
      
      ##### select which assays from which are sig assoc with TOA in at least one group
      
      if(length(group_colors_to_use) == 2){
        ### make corr_df_combo wider
        corr_df_combo_wide_tr <- corr_df_combo %>%
          ## remove redundant columns
          dplyr::select(-Time,-var_comp) %>%
          tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "Group",

          ### remove rows where dir is same for both groups
          dplyr::filter(dir_DNA != dir_ALVAC)
      }else{
        ### make corr_df_combo wider

          dplyr::select(-Time,-var_comp) %>%
          tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "Group",

          ### trim to only sig in at least one group
          dplyr::filter(rowname %in% rownames(cor_test_mat_for_plot))
      }
      
      ######## collect data to plot
      df_to_plot <- full_df %>%
        ## trim to only sig vars
        dplyr::select(!!!rlang::syms(c(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname,"TOA_adj","Group_f"))) %>%
        ### make longer

        ### factorize
        dplyr::mutate(ALFQA_only = factor(str_after_first(Group_simp,"_"),
                                          c("Alum","ALFQA")),
                      Group_simp = NULL)
      
      
      
      
      
      list_of_plots <- list()
      plotted_data_df <- data.frame()
      
      
      for (i in corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname){
        #### trim to only this variable
        curr_df_to_plot <- df_to_plot %>%

          p <-  ggplot(curr_df_to_plot, aes(y = value, 
                                            x = TOA_adj, fill = Group_f))+
            scale_fill_manual(name = paste0("Study (color)"), values=group_colors_to_use) +  
            scale_shape_manual(name=paste0("Adjuvant (shape)"), values=c(Alum=21,ALFQA=24)) +
            scale_color_manual(name = paste0("Study (color)"), values=group_colors_to_use) +
            
            geom_smooth(aes(color = Group_f), se = FALSE, method = "lm")+
            
            geom_point(aes(fill = Group_f, shape = ALFQA_only), 
                       color =  "black", size = 5, stroke = 1, alpha = 0.8, cex = 3)+
            
            # ### for exponent formatting
            #    scale_y_log10(breaks = trans_breaks("log10",function (x) 10^x),
            #                  limits = c(as.double(list_of_subsets_for_plotting[[paste0(set)]][i,"limit_y_low"]),
            #                                             as.double(list_of_subsets_for_plotting[[paste0(set)]][i,"limit_y_high"])),
            #                  labels = trans_format("log10",math_format(10^.x)),
            #                  ## for no expansion beyond limits
            #                  expand = c(0,0))+
            
            
            scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,12),
                               limits = c(0,12),
                               ## for no expansion beyond limits
                               expand = c(0,1))+
            
            ylab(paste0(y_line1,"\n",y_line2))+
            labs(title = paste0("studyA1: R=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"R_value_studyA1"]),2),
                                ", p=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"raw_p_studyA1"]),2),
                                ":  studyA2: R=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"R_value_studyA2"]),2),
                                ", p=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"raw_p_studyA2"]),2),
                                ":  studyB: R=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"R_value_studyB"]),2),
                                ", p=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"raw_p_studyB"]),2)),
                 
                 subtitle = paste0("studyC: R=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"R_value_studyC"]),2),
                                   ", p=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"raw_p_studyC"]),2),
                                   ";  studyD: R=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"R_value_studyD"]),2),
                                   ", p=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"raw_p_studyD"]),2),
                                   "studyE: R=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"R_value_studyE"]),2),
                                   ", p=",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$rowname == i),"raw_p_studyE"]),2))
            )+
            theme_bw()+
            #### change color in legend for fill to have shape that can fill
            guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21)))+
            
            theme(legend.position="right", 
                  panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  panel.border = element_blank(), 
                  axis.line = element_line(colour = "black",lineend = "square"),
                  axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
                  axis.text = element_text(size = 15),
                  plot.title =  element_text(size = 7#, color = group_colors_to_use[1]
                  ), 
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7#, color = group_colors_to_use[2]
                  ),
            )
          
          
          
          
          
          
          
        }
        p1 <- p
        list_of_plots[[i]] <- p1 + theme(legend.position="none")
        
        
        
        cat("\n")
        cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
        
        plotted_data_df <- rbind(plotted_data_df, curr_df_to_plot)
        
      }
      
      ### get the legend
      #https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13649473/add-a-common-legend-for-combined-ggplots
      g_legend<-function(a.gplot){
        tmp <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(a.gplot))
        leg <- which(sapply(tmp$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
        legend <- tmp$grobs[[leg]]
        return(legend)}
      
      ### empty filler
      # list_of_plots[[nrow(list_of_subsets_for_plotting[[paste0(set)]])+1]]<-ggplot() + theme_void()
      # list_of_plots[[nrow(list_of_subsets_for_plotting[[paste0(set)]])+2]]<-g_legend(p1) ### grabs from the last plot
      list_of_plots[[nrow(corr_df_combo_wide_tr)+1]]<-g_legend(p1) ### grabs from the last plot
      
      ### fill out to at least 9 empty plots 
      if(length(list_of_plots) < 12){
        for(curr_missing in (length(list_of_plots)+1):12){
          list_of_plots[[curr_missing]] <- ggplot() + theme_void()
        }
        
      }else{
        list_of_plots <- list_of_plots
      }
      
      do.call("grid.arrange",c(list_of_plots, ncol=num_columns_for_plot))
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
      
      
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
      
      list_of_plotted[[paste0(fig_name_to_use,"_",Corr_name_base,"_",curr_ds)]] <- plotted_data_df
      
      
      
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
      
      
      
      
      
      
    }
    cat("\n")
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
    
    
    
  }else{
    cat(" ",paste0("no variables with same animals as TOA"),"\n")
    cat('\n')
    
  }
  
  cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
  
  
  
}

cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
```

```{r AssocWithSelf, results='asis', fig.height=50, fig.width=15}
          p <-  ggplot(curr_df_to_plot, aes(y = !!rlang::sym(var_y), 
                                            x = !!rlang::sym(var_x), fill = Group_f))+
            scale_fill_manual(name = paste0("Vaccine (color)"), values=group_colors_to_use) +  
            scale_shape_manual(name=paste0("Adjuvant (shape)"), values=c(Alum=21,ALFQA=24)) +
            scale_color_manual(name = paste0("Vaccine (color)"), values=group_colors_to_use) +
            
            geom_smooth(aes(color = Group_f), se = FALSE, method = "lm")+
            
            geom_point(aes(fill = Group_f, shape = ALFQA_only), 
                       color =  "black", size = 5, stroke = 1, alpha = 0.8, cex = 3)+
            
            # ### for exponent formatting
            #    scale_y_log10(breaks = trans_breaks("log10",function (x) 10^x),
            #                  limits = c(as.double(list_of_subsets_for_plotting[[paste0(set)]][i,"limit_y_low"]),
            #                                             as.double(list_of_subsets_for_plotting[[paste0(set)]][i,"limit_y_high"])),
            #                  labels = trans_format("log10",math_format(10^.x)),
            #                  ## for no expansion beyond limits
            #                  expand = c(0,0))+
            
            
            
            xlab(paste0(x_line1,"\n",x_line2))+
            ylab(paste0(y_line1,"\n",y_line2))+
            labs(title = paste0("DNA: R = ",
                                signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$var2 == var_x &
                                                                               corr_df_combo_wide_tr$var1 == var_y),
                                                                       "R_value_DNA"]),2),
                                ", p = ",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$var2 == var_x &
                                                                                        corr_df_combo_wide_tr$var1 == var_y),"raw_p_DNA"]),2)),
                 subtitle = paste0("ALVAC: R = ",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$var2 == var_x &
                                                                                                corr_df_combo_wide_tr$var1 == var_y),"R_value_ALVAC"]),2),
                                   ", p = ",signif(as.double(corr_df_combo_wide_tr[which(corr_df_combo_wide_tr$var2 == var_x &
                                                                                           corr_df_combo_wide_tr$var1 == var_y),"raw_p_ALVAC"]),2)))+
            theme_bw()+
            #### change color in legend for fill to have shape that can fill
            guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21)))+
            
            theme(legend.position="right", 
                  panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  panel.border = element_blank(), 
                  axis.line = element_line(colour = "black",lineend = "square"),
                  axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
                  axis.text = element_text(size = 15),
                  plot.title =  element_text(size = 15, color = group_colors_to_use[1]), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15, color = group_colors_to_use[2]),
            )
          
          
          p1 <- p
          list_of_plots[[i]] <- p1 + theme(legend.position="none")
          
          
          
          cat("\n")
          cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
          
          plotted_data_df <- rbind(plotted_data_df, curr_df_to_plot %>%
                                     ### add comparison column and make colnames generic
                                     dplyr::mutate(comparison = paste0(var_x,"__vs__",var_y)) %>%
                                     dplyr::rename(var1_value = 4, var2_value = 5) %>%
                                     dplyr::relocate(comparison, .before = "var1_value")
          )
          
        }
        
        ### get the legend
        #https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13649473/add-a-common-legend-for-combined-ggplots
        g_legend<-function(a.gplot){
          tmp <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(a.gplot))
          leg <- which(sapply(tmp$grobs, function(x) x$name) == "guide-box")
          legend <- tmp$grobs[[leg]]
          return(legend)}
        
        ### empty filler
        # list_of_plots[[nrow(list_of_subsets_for_plotting[[paste0(set)]])+1]]<-ggplot() + theme_void()
        # list_of_plots[[nrow(list_of_subsets_for_plotting[[paste0(set)]])+2]]<-g_legend(p1) ### grabs from the last plot
        list_of_plots[[nrow(corr_df_combo_wide_tr)+1]]<-g_legend(p1) ### grabs from the last plot
        
        ### fill out to at least 9 empty plots 
        if(length(list_of_plots) < 12){
          for(curr_missing in (length(list_of_plots)+1):12){
            list_of_plots[[curr_missing]] <- ggplot() + theme_void()
          }
          
        }else{
          list_of_plots <- list_of_plots
        }
        
        do.call("grid.arrange",c(list_of_plots, ncol=num_columns_for_plot))
        
        cat("\n")
        cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
        
        
        
        cat("\n")
        cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
        
        list_of_plotted[[paste0(fig_name_to_use,"_",Corr_name_base,"_",curr_ds)]] <- plotted_data_df
        
        
        
        
        cat("\n")
        cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
        
        
        
        
        
      }
      
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
      
      
      
    }
    cat("\n")
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
    
  }else{
    cat(" ",paste0("no variables with same animals to compare"),"\n")
    cat('\n')
    
  }
  
  
  
  
  cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
  
  
  
}

cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
```

```{r vsADCCEff_prep}
cor_method <- "spearman"
Corr_name_base <- "VsADCCEff"

#### for corrplots
ann_pval_level <- 0.05
cl_ratio <- 0.5
pch_cex <- 2
tl_cex <- 0.8

###### for scatterplot
num_columns_for_plot <- 3


### trim to only the variables for this fig
curr_phen_long <- phen_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(variable %in% list_of_vars[[paste0(curr_var_set)]]) %>%
  ### remove naive animals
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("Naive",Group))


levels_vars_to_use <- c("Pct_CD14_efferocytes","Arif_ADCC_NCI05specific")
deltaFC_vars_to_use <- c("Pct_CD14_efferocytes","engulfing_capabiluity_MFI_CFSE")


#### collect ADCC & Eff to compare to
full_df_compare <- phen_long %>%
  ### first collect levels vars
  dplyr::filter(variable %in% levels_vars_to_use) %>%
  ### remove naive animals
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("Naive",Group))  %>%
  ## trim to only Animal_comp_time, var and curr_ds
  dplyr::select(c(Animal_comp_time,variable,amount)) %>%
  ## move comp and timepoint to var
  dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = str_before_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),
                var_comp_time = paste0(variable,"__",str_after_first(Animal_comp_time,"__")),
                Animal_comp_time = NULL,
                variable = NULL) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(var_comp_time) %>%
  ## make wider
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var_comp_time", values_from = "amount") %>%
  ## remove columns with only NA
  dplyr::select(where(function(x) !all(is.na(x)))) %>%
  
  #### add in FC for FC vars
  dplyr::full_join(phen_long %>%
                     ### first collect levels vars & remove baseline
                     dplyr::filter(variable %in% deltaFC_vars_to_use & Time_Point != "Baseline") %>%
                     
                     ### remove naive animals
                     dplyr::filter(!grepl("Naive",Group))  %>%
                     ## trim to only Animal_comp_time, var and curr_ds
                     dplyr::select(c(Animal_comp_time,variable,FC)) %>%
                     ## move comp and timepoint to var
                     dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = str_before_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),
                                   var_comp_time = paste0(variable,"__",str_after_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),"vsBaslineFC"),
                                   Animal_comp_time = NULL,
                                   variable = NULL) %>%
                     ## make wider
                     tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var_comp_time", values_from = "FC") %>%
                     ## remove columns with only NA
                     dplyr::select(where(function(x) !all(is.na(x)))),
                   by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  
  
  #### add in delta for delta vars
  dplyr::full_join(phen_long %>%
                     ### first collect levels vars & remove baseline
                     dplyr::filter(variable %in% deltaFC_vars_to_use & Time_Point != "Baseline") %>%
                     ### remove naive animals
                     dplyr::filter(!grepl("Naive",Group))  %>%
                     ## trim to only Animal_comp_time, var and curr_ds
                     dplyr::select(c(Animal_comp_time,variable,delta)) %>%
                     ## move comp and timepoint to var
                     dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = str_before_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),
                                   var_comp_time = paste0(variable,"__",str_after_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),"vsBaslineDelta"),
                                   Animal_comp_time = NULL,
                                   variable = NULL) %>%
                     ## make wider
                     tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var_comp_time", values_from = "delta") %>%
                     ## remove columns with only NA
                     dplyr::select(where(function(x) !all(is.na(x)))),
                   by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  
  
  ### add in group 
  dplyr::left_join(data.frame(unique(phen_long[,c("Sample_ID",group_var_to_use)])) %>%
                     dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = paste0("m",Sample_ID)) %>%
                     ### collapse rows and take first value ***need to see if this is correct**
                     dplyr::group_by(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use), Sample_ID) %>%
                     dplyr::reframe(across(everything(), ~ dplyr::first(.))) %>% 
                     ungroup(), 
                   by = "Sample_ID") %>%
  dplyr::rename(Group_to_use=!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Sample_ID") %>%
  ### factorize group
  dplyr::mutate(Group_f = factor(Group_to_use, intersect(
    names(group_colors_to_use),
    unique(data.frame(curr_phen_long)[,group_var_to_use])))) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Group_to_use)
```

```{r AssocWithADCCEff, results='asis', fig.height=8, fig.width=9}

### for each dataset type

for(curr_ds in ds_to_use){
  cat("#### ",paste0(curr_ds," {.tabset}"),"\n")
  cat('\n')
  
  
  Corr_name <- paste0(Corr_name_base,"_",curr_var_set,"_",curr_ds)
  
  ## full_df only has the variables in columns and the factorized group (plus any other covariates if they are in the model)
  
  full_df <- curr_phen_long %>%
    ## trim to only Animal_comp_time, var and curr_ds
    dplyr::select(c(Animal_comp_time,variable, !!rlang::sym(curr_ds))) %>%
    ## move comp and timepoint to var
    dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = str_before_first(Animal_comp_time,"__"),
                  var_comp_time = paste0(variable,"__",str_after_first(Animal_comp_time,"__")),
                  Animal_comp_time = NULL,
                  variable = NULL) %>%
    ## make wider
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var_comp_time", values_from = all_of(curr_ds)) %>%
    ## remove columns with only NA
    dplyr::select(where(function(x) !all(is.na(x)))) %>%
    ### add in group 
    dplyr::left_join(data.frame(unique(phen_long[,c("Sample_ID",group_var_to_use)])) %>%
                       dplyr::mutate(Sample_ID = paste0("m",Sample_ID)) %>%
                       ### collapse rows and take first value ***need to see if this is correct**
                       dplyr::group_by(!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use), Sample_ID) %>%
                       dplyr::reframe(across(everything(), ~ dplyr::first(.))) %>% 
                       ungroup(), 
                     by = "Sample_ID") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Group_to_use=!!rlang::sym(group_var_to_use)) %>%
    column_to_rownames("Sample_ID") %>%
    ### factorize group
    dplyr::mutate(Group_f = factor(Group_to_use, intersect(
      names(group_colors_to_use),
      unique(data.frame(curr_phen_long)[,group_var_to_use])))) %>%
    dplyr::select(-Group_to_use)
  
  
  
  
  
  #### there need to be some variables
  if(dim(full_df)[2] > 2){
    
    ### for each group separately
    ### prep to collect
    corr_df_combo <- data.frame()
    
    for(curr_group in names(group_colors_to_use)){
      
      
      #curr_df1: rows = samples, columns = variables
      #curr_df2: rows = samples, columns = TAO
      
      curr_df1 <- full_df %>%
        ## filter to only this group
        dplyr::filter(Group_f == curr_group) %>%
        ## filter to only the common animals
        rownames_to_column() %>%
        dplyr::filter(rowname %in% intersect(unique(rowname),rownames(full_df_compare))) %>%
        column_to_rownames() %>%
        ## trim to only the variable columns
        dplyr::select(-c(Group_f))
      
      curr_df2 <- full_df_compare %>%
        ## filter to only this group
        dplyr::filter(Group_f == curr_group) %>%
        ## filter to only the common animals
        rownames_to_column() %>%
        dplyr::filter(rowname %in% intersect(unique(rowname),rownames(curr_df1))) %>%
        column_to_rownames() %>%
        ## trim to only the variable columns
        dplyr::select(-c(Group_f))
      
      
      sp <- psych::corr.test(as.matrix(signif(curr_df1,7)), as.matrix(signif(curr_df2,7)), method = cor_method,
                             use="pairwise",
                             adjust="none",ci=FALSE)
      
      cor_mat <- sp$r
      cor_test_mat <- data.frame(sp$p)
      
      ## no adj p for multiple comparisons by BH over assays since never symmetric
      # cor_test_adj_mat <- cor_test_mat #duplicate dataframe to replace values
      # for(curr_assay in colnames(curr_df1)) {
      #   cor_test_adj_mat[curr_assay,] <- p.adjust(cor_test_mat[curr_assay,], method = "BH")
      # }
      # 
      #  
      #### also combine to dataframe since only one columns
      corr_df <- dplyr::left_join(data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
                                    rownames_to_column("var1") %>%
                                    ##make longer
                                    tidyr::pivot_longer(!var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "R_value"),
                                  data.frame(cor_test_mat) %>%
                                    rownames_to_column("var1") %>%
                                    ##make longer
                                    tidyr::pivot_longer(!var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "raw_p"),
                                  by = c("var1","var2")) %>%
        ### add columns
        dplyr::mutate(
          ### set R_value to NA if p is NA i.e there were only 2 datapoints, some how the R is calculated but the p is not
          R_value = ifelse(is.na(raw_p),NA,R_value),
          
          #### for p < ann_pval_level
          dir = ifelse(R_value > 0 & raw_p < ann_pval_level,
                       "up", 
                       ifelse(R_value < 0 & raw_p < ann_pval_level,
                              "down","not_sig")),
          Group = paste0(curr_group))# %>%
      #### remove self correlations ---> none since comparing to olink
      #  dplyr::filter(var1 != var2)
      
      
      corr_df_combo <- rbind(corr_df_combo, corr_df)
      
    }
    
    # ### if FC or delta, remove baselines
    # if(curr_ds != "amount"){
    #   corr_df_combo <- corr_df_combo %>% 
    #     dplyr::filter(Time != "Baseline")
    # }
    # 
    ### save stats
    list_of_stats[[paste0(Corr_name_base,"_",str_remove_all(curr_var_set,"_columns"),"_",
                          substring(curr_ds,1,2) ## trim to 2 letters since too long for excel tab name
    )]] <- corr_df_combo
    
    # saveRDS(corr_df_combo, file = file.path(outputRData_dir, 
    #                                                               paste0(Corr_name,"_", cor_method,"_CoefPvals_untrimmed.rds")))
    
    
    cat("\n")
    cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
    
    
    ################## now plot sig correlations for all groups
    
    
    
    
    cor_test_mat_for_plot <- corr_df_combo %>%
      ### trim to only p values
      dplyr::select(var1,var2,raw_p,Group) %>%
      ## replace NaN with na
      dplyr::mutate(raw_p = ifelse(is.nan(raw_p),NA,raw_p)) %>%
      ##  combine var2 and group
      dplyr::mutate(var2_group = paste0(var2,"__",Group),
                    var2 = NULL,
                    Group = NULL) %>%
      ## make wider
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var2_group",values_from = "raw_p") %>%
      column_to_rownames("var1") %>%
      ## filter to only vars that are sig in at least one group
      dplyr::filter_at(vars(everything(.)), any_vars(. < ann_pval_level)) %>%
      as.matrix() 
    
    cor_mat_for_plot <- corr_df_combo %>%
      ### trim to only p values
      dplyr::select(var1,var2,R_value,Group) %>%
      ##  combine var2 and group
      dplyr::mutate(var2_group = paste0(var2,"__",Group),
                    var2 = NULL,
                    Group = NULL) %>%
      ## make wider
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "var2_group",values_from = "R_value") %>%
      ### filter to only sig vars
      dplyr::filter(var1 %in% rownames(cor_test_mat_for_plot)) %>%
      column_to_rownames("var1") %>%
      as.matrix()
    
    cl_ratio <- 0.2
    # pch_cex <- .6
    # tl_cex <- 0.1
    alluvial_text <- 3
    
    if(length(which(cor_test_mat_for_plot <  as.numeric(ann_pval_level))) == 0){
      
      
      cat(" ",paste0("no variables with p < ",ann_pval_level),"\n")
      cat('\n')
      
      
    }else{
      
      
      cat("##### ",paste0("corrplot"),"\n")
      cat("\n")
      #### otherwise can use the stars
      corrplot::corrplot(cor_mat_for_plot, method = 'square', 
                         is.corr = FALSE, #since not symmetric
                         p.mat = cor_test_mat_for_plot,
                         sig.level = as.numeric(ann_pval_level), 
                         insig='label_sig',  #set p < 0.05 to blank
                         pch.cex = pch_cex, pch.col = 'white',tl.col = 'black',tl.cex=tl_cex,
                         ##legend
                         cl.ratio = cl_ratio, #cl.cex = 2,
                         #addCoef.col ='grey80', 
                         #number.cex = 0.5, #add corr coeff to sig circles
                         #order = order, ## CANNOT ORDER ASSYMMETRIC
                         col = (COL2('PuOr',1000)), ##make orange NEGATIVE
                         col.lim = c(-1,1) ##set limits to be the same across plots
                         # title = vaccine_groups[i], mar=c(0,0,1,0) # http://stackoverflow.com/a/14754408/54964
      )
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
      
      
      
      ########## add alluvials
      
      
      
      df_for_alluvials <- corr_df_combo %>%
        ## simplify variable by combining var1 and varw
        dplyr::mutate(variable = paste0(var1,"__vs__",var2),
                      ### add dir
                      dir = ifelse(raw_p < ann_pval_level, 
                                   ifelse(R_value > 0, "pos","neg"),
                                   "not_sig")) %>%
        
        #        ### also remove inverse duplicates
        #        group_by(grp = paste(pmax(var1, var2), pmin(var1, var2), sep = "_")) %>%
        # dplyr::filter(row_number() == 1) %>%
        # ungroup() %>%
        # dplyr::select(-grp) %>%
        dplyr::select(-c(raw_p,R_value,var1,var2))  %>%
        
        ### remove notsig for all groups
        ## make wider
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "Group", values_from = "dir") %>%
        column_to_rownames("variable") %>%
        ## remove rows if all not_sig 
        dplyr::filter_all(any_vars(. != "not_sig")) %>%
        ## also remove if all na
        dplyr::filter_all(any_vars(!is.na(.))) %>%
        ### back to long
        rownames_to_column("variable") %>%
        tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = !variable, names_to = "Group", values_to = "dir") %>%
        ## factorize
        dplyr::mutate(Group = factor(Group, names(group_colors_to_use)),
                      dir = factor(dir, c("pos","not_sig","neg")),
                      variable = factor(variable)) %>%
        ## arrange
        dplyr::arrange(dir, variable, Group)
      
      
      color_df <- data.frame("group"=unique(levels(df_for_alluvials$dir)),
                             "color"=c("purple","grey","orange"),
                             "outline"=c("black","black","black"))
      
      curr_color_df <- color_df[which(color_df$group %in% unique(df_for_alluvials$dir)),]
      
      
      cat("##### ",paste0("alluvial"),"\n")
      cat("\n")
      
      gg <- ggplot(df_for_alluvials,
                   aes(x = Group, stratum = dir, alluvium = variable))+
        stat_alluvium(aes(fill = dir), width = 1/2, alpha = 1/2,) +
        stat_stratum(aes(stratum = dir, fill = dir), width = 1/2) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = curr_color_df$color)+
        stat_alluvium(geom = "text", aes(label = variable), size = alluvial_text, show.legend = FALSE) + ## to label NA category
        stat_alluvium(geom = "text", aes(label = variable, color = dir), size = alluvial_text, show.legend = FALSE) +
        
        scale_color_manual(values = curr_color_df$outline)+
        theme_bw()+
        labs(fill = paste0(cor_method," p < ", ann_pval_level, " R direction"))
      
      plot(gg)
      
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
      
      
      
      
      cat("\n")
      cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!
      
      
      cat("##### ",paste0("table"),"\n")
      cat("\n")
      
      
      to_print <- corr_df_combo %>%
        ## simplify variable by combining var1 and varw
        dplyr::mutate(variable = paste0(var1,"__vs__",var2),
                      var1_time = str_after_last(var1,"__"),
                      var1 = str_before_last(var1,"__"),
                      var2_time = str_after_last(var2,"__"),
                      var2 = str_before_last(var2,"__"),
                      
                      ### add dir
                      dir = ifelse(raw_p < ann_pval_level, 
                                   ifelse(R_value > 0, "pos","neg"),
                                   "not_sig")) %>%
        #### trim to variables in alluvial
        dplyr::filter(variable %in% df_for_alluvials$variable) %>%
        dplyr::select(-variable) %>%
        ## make wider to put the groups on the same line
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "Group", values_from = c("raw_p","R_value","dir")) %>%
        DT::datatable(extensions = 'Buttons',
                      options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                                     buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
                                     iDisplayLength = 25,
                                     lengthMenu = list(c(10,25,50,-1),

      #) , height = "100%", width = "100%")
```
